title: Restore a wallet from its recovery phrase

summary.text: On mainnet, Daedalus restores a Daedalus wallet from a 12-word or 24-word recovery phrase, a paper wallet from a 27-word recovery phrase, and a Yoroi wallet from a 15-word recovery phrase. A hardware wallet is paired, not restored.

problem.text: A user wants to restore a wallet in Daedalus and needs to know what the restoration requires.

symptoms.text: The user needs to restore a wallet and is unsure what to prepare.

user_phrases.text: How do I restore my wallet?

daedalus.notes: Behavior read from the Daedalus 11.6.0 release notes and the 11.6.0 tag source. Check a newer release before relying on it for a later version.

causes.claim: The available evidence does not establish one cause.

resolutions.action: Select Daedalus wallet for a Daedalus wallet or a paper wallet, or Yoroi wallet for a Yoroi wallet.
resolutions.why: Daedalus restores a paper wallet as a Daedalus wallet.

resolutions.action: For a Daedalus wallet or a paper wallet, select the option with the number of words in your recovery phrase, which for a paper wallet is 27 words - paper wallet (Byron legacy wallet), and select Continue.
resolutions.why: The wallet kind and word count decide how Daedalus reads the recovery phrase.

resolutions.action: For a Yoroi wallet, select 15 words (Byron legacy wallet) or 15 words (Shelley wallet), and select Continue.
resolutions.why: Daedalus restores the first as a Byron legacy wallet and the second as a Shelley wallet. The two derive different addresses from the same recovery phrase.

resolutions.action: Enter your recovery phrase and select Check recovery phrase.
resolutions.why: Daedalus checks the phrase before it restores the wallet.

resolutions.action: Enter a wallet name and a spending password, and select Continue. Neither needs to match the ones you used before.
resolutions.why: Wallet names and spending passwords are stored only on the computer.

expected_outcome.text: The restored wallet appears in Daedalus with the funds and transaction history of the original wallet.

prerequisites: The recovery phrase of the wallet you want to restore, and the number of words it has.
No other restoration in progress: Daedalus restores one wallet at a time.
consequences: If you enter a hardware wallet's recovery phrase here instead of pairing the device, its private keys are exposed to the risks of this computer.
The wallet name and spending password you set are stored only on this computer, not on the blockchain.
recovery: If the restored wallet is empty or lacks funds you expected, check the recovery phrase and restore again with the right one.

If a restored Yoroi wallet is empty or lacks funds you expected, restore it again with the other 15-word option. The two options make wallets with different addresses from the same recovery phrase, and the first wallet stays in Daedalus.
If you close the restore window before you finish, nothing is saved and you start again.

evidence.rationale: Release notes, tagged source and portal pages directly state the behavior; this is source inspection, not runtime testing.

faq.reason: Common support topic with a short answer that every cited source supports.
